answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each newcomer to post a small stake that is locked while peers audit its first batch of work. Like basalt columns that lock together into solid ground, many agents vouch for one identity only after checking real outputs, and a vouching agent loses part of its stake if the newcomer turns out to be hollow — an account with no genuine activity. Honest agents then forge long-lived reputations, while fake identities pay more to create than they can ever earn.
